subject: Acme - Context length & token volume for pricing (follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Acme — context length & token volume (post-call recap)

Hi Alex / Sara — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can get you a pricing sketch that matches usage patterns.

Call recap (key points):
- Primary use case: long-form document summarization + extractive Q&A for internal research + a daily end-of-day analytics report.
- Latency tolerance: interactive for Q&A (sub-second preferred for short queries), batch OK for the end-of-day jobs.
- Data sensitivity: mostly internal, some regulated PII downstream (we discussed Private options).

Token profile (what you shared today):
- Avg prompt tokens: ~120 tokens (templates + user context)
- Avg completion tokens: ~520 tokens (summaries and extracts)
- 8k context needed for ~15% of calls (doc-level summaries)
- 32k context needed for ~5% of calls (long reports / stitched docs)
- 128k context needed for <1% (monthly batch analyses / archive scans)

Estimated monthly volume (rough ballpark from the call):
- Prompt tokens: ~40M / month
- Completion tokens: ~150M / month
- Total tokens: ~190M / month

Budget & unit economics:
- You mentioned a target spend range of roughly $6k–$12k / month while evaluating initial deployment.
- You also said you’d be happiest if unit economics landed near $/1M tokens in the low-mid double digits (your target noted roughly $30–$45 per 1M tokens).

Next steps I need from you to make the pricing sketch tighter:
1) Can you confirm the avg prompt/completion numbers above (or share a small sample / CSV)? attaching a token_profile.csv template — please fill if possible.
2) Confirm percent of requests that need 8k / 32k / 128k (the rough splits above are OK if that’s easier).
3) Confirm whether you prefer an initial Hosted POC or would consider a short Dedicated pilot (committed capacity) — both have different unit economics.

I’ll draft two pricing options once we have the profile: (A) Hosted PAYG and (B) 3-month committed pilot (Dedicated) with lower $/1M token pricing and SLA.

Attaching: acme-token-profile.csv (schema + example rows).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the pricing sketches once you confirm the numbers.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme — context length & token volume (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa — this is great. A couple of clarifications / corrections from our side:
- Avg prompt tokens look closer to ~200 (we have longer templates + user history).
- Avg completion tokens are closer to ~750 for summaries (we aim for a bit more verbose outputs).
- The 8k / 32k splits are probably higher: 8k ~20% of calls, 32k ~10%. 128k remains rare (~0.5–1%).

Updated monthly estimate (based on clarified averages):
- Prompt tokens: ~120M / month
- Completion tokens: ~450M / month
- Total tokens: ~570M / month

Budget context: we’re looking at a realistic range of $20k–$40k / month for the initial rollout (we can tighten if we see better unit economics).

I’ll try to export a 1-week sample and drop it in the CSV you attached by tomorrow. Also open to a short committed pilot if the numbers make sense.

— Alex
Product Lead, Research Tools
Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme — context length & token volume (post-call recap)

Alex — perfect, that update helps a lot. Based on the clarified profile (total ~570M tokens / month with the 8k/32k tail you noted), here are the two sketch pricing options I’ll formalize into an MOP / SOW:

Option A — Hosted (PAYG) — quick POC
- Unit price: ~$65 per 1M tokens (hosted catalog models with standard throughput)
- For 570M tokens/month that maps to ~ $37k / month (est).
- Pros: fastest onboarding, no infra commitments; Cons: higher nominal $/1M.

Option B — 3-month Committed Pilot (Dedicated reserved capacity)
- Committed discount: ~$30 per 1M tokens (reserved GPU capacity, discounted unit economics)
- For 570M tokens/month that maps to ~ $17k / month (est) — plus a small infra reservation fee and minimum commit.
- Pros: lower unit cost, predictable performance + SLA.

Notes on context-length pricing:
- 8k vs 32k vs 128k primarily affects model selection and memory footprint; for Dedicated we can allocate GPUs/instances that make 32k and occasional 128k runs much cheaper relative to Hosted wide-margin pricing.
- We’ll also propose an optimization plan (prefix caching + batching for batch jobs and tuned quantized variants) to drive unit economics down over time — I’ll include estimated savings in the SOW.

Next steps:
1) I’ll upload a short Mutual Action Plan + initial SOW outlining the two options (attaching mutual-action-plan.docx).
2) Once you drop the 1-week sample in the CSV I can run a quick token-profile calc and firm the numbers.
> 3) If you want, we can schedule a 30-min pricing-review slot with our solutions architect this week to go over the Dedicated pilot sizing.

If the committed option lands near your target $/1M (you mentioned ~$30–$45), Option B will likely be the better path. I’ll send the SOW + MOP in the next email.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme — context length & token volume (post-call recap)

Quick note from me: I agree with proposing both options but recommend calling out a 3-month minimum commit for the Dedicated pilot and a clear exit metric (e.g., cost per 1M tokens and 95th pct latency) so both sides have measurable success criteria.

Also: we should include an optimization milestone at month 2 (batching + quantization) with target savings of ~20–30% on token spend for heavy batch workloads — that makes the Dedicated economics even stronger.

If you’re good, I’ll review the SOW before it goes out.

Jonas
VP Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
